If I were to allow a player to do this (which I probably would, because I mean come on now, spider riding hobbits halflings!!), this is what I'd do:

Anytime you went upside down or where climbing walls, you'd make all attacks and disadvantage. Then, I'd have you take the Mounted Combatant feat, but replace the "advantage on targets smaller than you" part with "can shoot while upside down without being at disadvantage."

Or we can just replace it with: Actions while mounted do not have disadvantage that is caused from being mounted.

This way, if I need to replace my spider with something else in case it dies (probably won't with Mounted Combatant) then the affect will still be viable.

I'd counter though that riding a spider is a very specific skill set compared to riding in general (horses, mules, oxen, etc.). You would have to have trained to shoot upside down, sideways, etc. because of the spider being able to do spider-y things, hence why I'd make such a specific change to the feat. :)

Right, but if you could ride a spider upside down, then anything else would probably be a breeze, which is why I think there shouldn't be any disadvantages while riding with this setup.
